result.summary: Yes, the tenant needed a reply. In event 006 they said the suggested settings didn't help, the oven hasn't worked since they moved in, and they asked for someone to come and inspect it. The landlord has no recorded spend limit, so I emailed the landlord asking them to approve an engineer to inspect it. I also replied to the tenant to say what happens next. A hold is set to chase the landlord in 2 days.
result.situation: The tenant reported the oven is not heating properly. Food such as chips or nuggets is still uncooked after 1.5 hours. The agency (Oliver) sent the tenant a manual and suggested settings. The tenant replied that these didn't help, the oven has never worked since they moved in, and they want someone to inspect it. No contractor, approval or cost is on record. The ticket says 'provider_selection', but no landlord approval exists.

judgement.why_this_decision: Event 006 shows the workaround from event 003 failed and the tenant asked for an inspection, so they were owed a reply. Classify_reply marked the message as routine ('auto'): the oven is still broken and there is no safety concern. Classify_intake says this is an urgent appliance repair that needs landlord approval. The landlord's profile has no pre-approved spend limit and no preferred channel, so I asked for approval by email (the default). I did not assign a contractor because there is no approval yet and no landlord authority on record.
